Workbook Projects

Production KPI DashboardExcel · Power Query · Pivot Table · Month Slicer · Production, target vs actual, loss, downtime, OEE and dispatch reporting.
Original dashboard walkthrough video — play directly here.

How the dashboard is built

Power Query: Monthly production data is brought into a consistent structure, cleaned/transformed, and refreshed when new monthly records are added. Use Excel Data → Refresh All according to the workbook's configured source.

Pivot Tables: Refreshed records are summarized for production, target, loss, downtime, runtime, OEE and dispatch. Use Sum for totals and Average for rate/percentage KPIs where appropriate.

Month Slicer: Select a month to filter connected Pivot Tables and linked dashboard views, making month-wise performance comparison easier.

Monthly update cycle: Add the new month's records to the configured source, keep the same column structure, run Refresh All, and refresh Pivot Tables if they are not set to refresh automatically.

Production Control & Tracking WorkbookOne Excel for One Department · Centralized Production Operations & Reporting

One Excel for One Department. No Other Excel Required. A consolidated Production Department workbook that brings the department’s daily records, analysis and reporting together in one place. The Master Sheet gives a central view, while dedicated sheets organize the detailed activities.

What it includes: Master Sheet, Production Tracking, GSM, Loss Analysis, Downtime / Breakdown Analysis, RM Reservation, Pallet Sheet, Lot Sheet, Daily Posting, Dispatch and Roster.

Business value: Instead of maintaining 4–5 separate Excel files for the same department, production information and supporting activities are managed in one structured workbook. This reduces scattered records and makes production status, losses, downtime, material reservations, pallet/lot movement and dispatch easier to track.

Master Sheet: Acts as the central department overview, bringing key information together so users can review the department’s operational position without switching between multiple workbooks.
